how_it_works: free space = cells a LiDAR ray crossed, farther than the robot's half-width from any map point; nothing unseen is drivable
plant aisles = long narrow free corridors in the map's wall direction with layered sides (stems, bed edge, next row); dock = where the robot was switched on
mission order = Rural Postman Problem on the graph of aisle ends + dock (every chosen aisle a required edge driven end to end, A* distances between ends), exact up to 7 aisles, ~0.1 s on the robot
HERMES (the agent's vision model) sees the plan drawn on the map with every leg's metres and the alternatives, and approves or changes the order before the robot moves
every leg planned by A* on the free grid from the believed pose (clearance cost -> middle of the aisle); survey legs planned inside the aisle

inside a row no pictures are asked for: odometry carries the belief; at every doorway (row <-> open), if the LiDAR still keeps a twin place alive, the agent decides from the whole situation (both places with the fit of the current scan AND of the whole drive so far - one scan every 2 m over the last 80 m placed at each candidate place - metres driven, doors passed, verdicts so far, the plan, live view vs both reference views)

while driving: belief checked against every scan; whole-map search every 10 m keeps rivals; a belief that stops fitting, a rival clearly better over 2 m, or an obstacle where the map says free while the scans do not fit -> new anchor, odometry history re-placed, records relabelled, mission re-derived from the full goal list
an obstacle where the map says free while the scans DO fit = something new: marked on the grid, path planned around it
off the planned path by > 1 m -> planned again; no candidate can plan -> step 2 m into open space and search again; no progress for 40 rounds -> search again
before docking: live view vs the dock vs up to two far rivals (>= 15 m away); a verdict that moves the robot is asked twice

the whole-drive fit is the walls the robot already passed: one scan inside a row fits both twin houses, the drive with its doorways, yards and row ends (the two rows differ by 1.6 m) fits one house; it vetoes a camera verdict at the dock that would move the belief against it

a blocked way changes the mission, not the belief: a row whose mouth is blocked is entered from its other end; a goal that cannot be reached is left out and reported; a row counts as surveyed once the robot's own path has covered >= 50 % of its stops, otherwise it is driven again from this end
caveats: LiDAR scans are synthetic (ray-cast on the self-built map); no sensor noise
the live camera view stands in from the look-around image set, >= 1.5 m from the reference image
only the aisles the robot drove during the led drive are seen empty; the two side aisles are known from their ends and left out of the mission
two identical houses and two yards make the farm nearly symmetric for a 2-D LiDAR; doorways and yards are where the pictures differ, rows are not
an aisle counts as covered when the robot's true path passed within 0.6 m of >= 98 % of its 0.45 m stops; the records are 'right' when house and metre agree with the truth within 1 m
